Rupture faite en déchirant, en se déchirant.

examples.text: La déchirure d’une plaie.

glosses: Trou résultant de cette rupture.

examples.text: Se riant de la liche, il saisit une page du grimoire et la déchira, certain d'avoir découvert le secret. Une nouvelle déchirure apparut dans la cape élimée de la liche.
— L’horizon était bouché dans le Nord, et c’est dans une déchirure de la brume que nous aperçûmes la base de l’île Jan-Mayen, […].
Pas question de mettre en péril la belle campagne des législatives en laissant paraître les déchirures internes post-présidentielles.

glosses: Déchirure musculaire.
To rend (a solid material) by holding or restraining in two places and pulling apart, whether intentionally or not; to destroy or separate.

examples.text: He tore his coat on the nail.

Then there came a reg'lar terror of a sou'wester same as you don't get one summer in a thousand, and blowed the shanty flat and ripped about half of the weir poles out of the sand. We spent consider'ble money getting 'em reset, and then a swordfish got into the pound and tore the nets all to slathers, right in the middle of the squiteague season.
He suffered, poor man, at seeing her so badly dressed, with laceless boots, and the arm-holes of her pinafore torn down to the hips; for the charwoman took no care of her.

glosses: To injure as if by pulling apart.

examples.text: He tore some muscles in a weight-lifting accident.

glosses: To destroy or reduce abstract unity or coherence, such as social, political or emotional.

examples.text: He was torn by conflicting emotions.

glosses: To make (an opening) with force or energy.

examples.text: A piece of debris tore a tiny straight channel through the satellite.
His boss will tear him a new one when he finds out.
The artillery tore a gap in the line.

glosses: To remove by tearing, or with sudden great force.

examples.text: Tear the coupon out of the newspaper.
[A] surge of muddy water tore him free from his sandy nook and tumbled him down the gully.

glosses: To demolish.

examples.text: The slums were torn down to make way for the new development.

glosses: To become torn, especially accidentally.

examples.text: My dress has torn.

glosses: To move or act with great speed, energy, or violence.

examples.text: He went tearing down the hill at 90 miles per hour.
The tornado lingered, tearing through town, leaving nothing upright.
He tore into the backlog of complaints.
I waited to hear no more, but tore up the village to find Poirot.
I've been tearing around in my fucking nightgown. 24/7 Sylvia Plath.

glosses: To smash or enter something with great force.

examples.text: The chain shot tore into the approaching line of infantry.

glosses: To be interrupted midway through.

glosses: A hole or break caused by tearing.

examples.text: A small tear is easy to mend, if it is on the seam.

glosses: A rampage.

examples.text: Big tears streamed from Lisa's eyes, rolling down her cheeks.
